question_text: What causes "shark fin" waveforms on the rising edge of an I2C bus, and how do you fix it?
answer_text: The RC time constant is too high (too much bus capacitance or weak pull-up resistors). Fix it by: 1) Decreasing the pull-up resistor values, or 2) Lowering the I2C clock speed.
explanation_text: I2C is open-drain, relying passively on resistors to pull the line high. High capacitance slows this rise time. Lowering the resistor speeds it up, but draws more current.
bonus_question_text: What is the trade-off of using smaller pull-up resistors?
bonus_answer_text: Higher power consumption, and the driving IC might struggle to pull the line fully low (below V_IL).
